record.original_question: Whenever there exists a rooted amalgamation of polytopes P and Q, must there also exist a universal rooted amalgamation of P and Q that covers every other rooted amalgamation of that pair?

evidence.quote: Problem 16. If there is a rooted amalgamation of the polytopes P and Q, then is there always a universal rooted amalgamation of P and Q?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let P and Q be abstract polytopes. A rooted polytope is a polytope together with a distinguished base flag. A rooted amalgamation of (rooted) polytopes P and Q is a rooted polytope R that covers both P and Q (i.e., admits flag-preserving surjections onto each, compatible with the chosen base flags). A universal rooted amalgamation of P and Q is a rooted amalgamation U of P and Q such that every rooted amalgamation R of P and Q is covered by U (equivalently, U is a maximal element with this covering property, with every other rooted amalgamation being a quotient of U).

Prove or disprove: whenever there exists at least one rooted amalgamation of P and Q, there exists a universal rooted amalgamation of P and Q that covers every other rooted amalgamation of the pair.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as one of 35 open problems in the 2016/2018 list on k-orbit polytopes. No subsequent publication resolving the existence of a universal rooted amalgamation under the stated hypothesis was found in the search results.
